body.heading: The invisible workforce of a day
paragraphs: Run through yesterday and count the people whose work made it run: the driver, the cleaner, the person who stocked the shelf and emptied the bin. Most days we interact with their work constantly and with them barely at all.
Being overlooked is its own quiet burden. People in background roles often say the same thing: whole days pass without anyone using their name or looking up.

body.heading: Small recognitions, real weight
paragraphs: Learn a name where you can — the regular driver, the office cleaner — and use it. Eye contact plus a specific thanks ('thanks for keeping this place running') takes five seconds.
If a service made your day, say so to the company as well as the person; praise that reaches a manager can matter at review time. Kindness with a paper trail is kindness squared.

description: Cleaners, drivers, night-shift staff, the person who refills the water — a thank-you aimed at the overlooked lands like a spotlight.
